steps.title: The Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how has your skin been since you finished your treatments with us? I usually hear one of three things. Still looking firm, a little starting to loosen up, or pretty much back to how it was. Which one is closest for you?

(Only three answers. Tap the one you hear.)

steps.title: Doing Great
steps.content:
That's great to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. Your notes say it was really bothering you before we started. Is it nice not to notice it in the mirror anymore?

(Let them answer.)

steps.title: Starting to Loosen Up
steps.content:
That happens, {{contact_first_name}}. Skin keeps changing, and results loosen up once treatments stop. It's not anything you did wrong. Your notes say you were really happy with how it turned out. What kept you from coming back in?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. Do not book yet.)

steps.title: Pretty Much Back to Before
steps.content:
I'm sorry to hear that, {{contact_first_name}}. Skin keeps changing, and results loosen up once treatments stop. It's not anything you did wrong. Your notes say you were really happy with the results. Was it cost, timing, or something else that kept you from coming back?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. Do not book yet.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm updating your file anyway. Can I ask you a few questions about anything else you've noticed?

(Wait for the yes. It's their file, so almost everyone says yes.)

steps.title: The Transition: Ask Permission
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, you said the area we treated is starting to loosen up again. We'll come back to that. First, can I ask you a few quick questions so your file is up to date?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down every area they name. You'll recap them in a moment.)

First, your jawline and neck. Any loosening there, the kind you catch in photos from the side?

How about your arms, any thin-looking skin there?

What about just above the knees?

And your chest?

How about the backs of your hands?

If your weight has changed since we saw you, are there areas where the skin didn't keep up?

(Recap what you wrote down, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, of those areas, which one would you most like to firm up?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(They already named one area. Write down every area they name, including that one.)

First, your jawline and neck. Any loosening there, the kind you catch in photos from the side?

How about your arms, any thin-looking skin there?

What about just above the knees?

And your chest?

How about the backs of your hands?

If your weight has changed since we saw you, are there areas where the skin didn't keep up?

(Recap everything, including what they mentioned at the start, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, between what you mentioned earlier and these, which one would you most like to firm up?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'd like to ask a few quick questions about {{main_concern}} so your file is up to date. It'll only take a minute.

(Ask these three questions in order. Pause after each and let them answer.)

How long has that been on your mind?

(Let them answer. Repeat it back.)

That's a long time to have something bothering you.

Is it something you notice here and there, or pretty much every time you look in the mirror?

(Let them answer.)

Think of a day you felt really good about how you looked. Now think of a day it really got to you. Do you have those two days in your head?

(Wait for the yes.)

On that harder day, how does it change things, like what you wear or how you feel around people?

(Let them open up. Do not rush.)

Thank you for sharing that. It makes sense, and it's something we help people with all the time.

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, it sounds like {{main_concern}} isn't just a small thing. It may be affecting how comfortable you feel around people. Do you see how that could be the case?

(Wait for the answer. If they hesitate, say "That's fair. It's clearly been on your mind, and that's reason enough." Then continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you in so {{provider_name}} can take a look at {{main_concern}}. If we can help, we'll tell you. If it's not the right fit, we'll tell you that too. Does that sound reasonable?

(Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: They Hesitate: Find Out Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, you said {{main_concern}} is something you'd like to feel better about. I don't want to assume anything. Is it the timing, or is something else holding you back?

(Stay easy about it. No pressure. Do not repeat the concern back at them. Let them answer.)

steps.title: Nothing Found: Why Did They Stop?
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm glad everything is still holding up so well.

Can I ask what changed that led you to stop coming in?

(Let them answer. Listen all the way through. Do not argue with it.)

The firmness you built does fade without a check-in now and then. A regular visit keeps it working for you. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in for a check-in so you keep the firmness you have. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Objection: “It loosened back up after I stopped”
steps.content:
That happens. Skin keeps changing once you're off treatments. That's why coming in makes sense, so we can look at the whole picture and make a plan.

Can we get you in so we can take a look?

steps.title: Objection: “I’m embarrassed it came back”
steps.content:
Please don't be. This happens to almost everyone once treatments stop. That's the reason we call. We'd just like to help you get back to where you were.

Would you be open to that?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Objection: “Did it even work last time?”
steps.content:
That's a fair question, and it's the kind of thing we'd want to talk through in person. That way we can look at the whole picture and see what would help it hold.

(Do not promise results on the call.)

Is there anything else on your mind?

steps.title: If They Say: “I was happy with my results”
steps.content:
That makes sense, {{contact_first_name}}, and that's the best reason there is. When you like what you see in the mirror, coming back stops feeling urgent. Looking that good is the result of the work we did together. The firmness you built does fade without a check-in now and then.

Does that make sense?

(Let them answer.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you back on the schedule so you keep looking this good. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: Cost or Budget
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}, and I'm glad you told me. Check-in visits are spaced out and cost a fraction of what it took to build the results. And you're not committing to anything. It's one visit so we can make sure everything is holding.

Does that seem fair?

(Let them answer.)

(Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts. The office handles that.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you back on the schedule. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: “Life got busy”
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Life fills up fast, and this kind of thing gets pushed down the list. It happens to everyone. A check-in visit is quick, and we can find a time that works around your schedule.

Would that work?

(Let them answer.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you back on the schedule at a time that's easy for you. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: “I’ll come back if it loosens again”
steps.content:
That's a fair way to think about it, {{contact_first_name}}. The one thing I'd share is that skin changes slowly. You usually don't notice until it's been sliding for a while. Keeping the results you have takes a lot less than rebuilding them.

Does that sound right?

(Let them answer.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you back on the schedule so we stay ahead of it. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: They Moved or Tried Another Provider
steps.content:
That's understandable, {{contact_first_name}}. Things change. If you're still in the area, we'd love to see you again. Your whole history is in your file, so we can pick up right where you left off.

Would that be okay?

(Let them answer.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you back on the schedule. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to think about it”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Can I ask what part you'd want to think over? Sometimes it's the cost, sometimes the timing, and sometimes people just want to be sure it's right for them.

(Listen. Their answer usually points to one of the buttons below. If it stays general, keep going.)

Coming in is really just information. You'd see what's possible and what it would involve, and then you decide with real answers. No pressure either way.

Does that help?

steps.title: Objection: “Just send me some info”
steps.content:
I'd be glad to send you some information, {{contact_first_name}}. The one thing I'd say is that a flyer can only tell you so much. It can't show you what's possible for you specifically. That's what a quick visit is for. So let me get you on the schedule first, and then I'll send the information along.

Does that work for you?
